To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the increased digitization of product innovations reshapes knowledge creation, assimilations and sharing in innovation network by redistributing control, increasing the need for knowledge coordination across space and time, and by stretching existing networks by increasing their reach and scope.

digitalization reshapes the nature of product innovation networks by redistributes control and increases the demand for knowledge integration across time and space, presenting novel challenges for innovation research.

digitalization of product innovation is changing the nature of innovation networks by increasing network connectivity, speed and scope of convergence, and knowledge heterogeneity, which, in turn, leads to the emergence of four types of innovation networks (project, clan, federated, anarchic).
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how the ongoing digitization of products and processes is reshaping knowledge creation and sharing within innovation networks.
the impact of digital technologies for the future of innovation networks.
the role of digital infrastructures and the emergence of new network forms in shaping the nature of knowledge creation and sharing within innovation networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the digital revolution is not a revolution at all. Rather it is a continuation of the industrial revolution, which has been ongoing since 1750.

digital product innovation is reshaping the nature and structure of innovation networks by increasing the scope, reach, speed and heterogeneity of knowledge creation and sharing, while at the same time, stretching existing innovation networks by increasing their need for control and knowledge coordination.
digital technologies are reshaping innovation networks, and the emerging innovation network forms are reshaping digital technologies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the digitization of products has changed the innovation network landscape and the nature of knowledge sharing in these networks.
we are in the midst of an innovation revolution that is fundamentally reshaping how we think, create and share knowledge.

we are witnessing the emergence of a new class of digital innovation networks, which we call anarchic innovation networks, that are founded on a new digital infrastructure that enables a more complete convergence of knowledge and a new form of innovation that we call digital product innovation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

digital technologies are not a panacea but rather a double-edged sword that increases innovation network connectivity and knowledge heterogeneity, which in turn increases the need for knowledge integration, coordination and control.
digital technologies are reshaping innovation networks by increasing their scope, reach and complexity, while simultaneously reducing their cost and increasing their speed.
the digital revolution is not just about technology. It is a social and cognitive revolution that is reshaping the way we innovate.
